pool.topic: Paper 3 Extended Investigation: Reduction Formulas, Wallis Integrals & Maclaurin Series
pool.q:
[AA HL Paper 3 Extended Investigation — 28 marks]
For \(n \in \mathbb{N}\), define the family of integrals \(I_n = \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^n x\,dx\).
(a) Evaluate \(I_0\), \(I_1\), and \(I_2\), giving exact answers in terms of \(\pi\) where appropriate. [4]
(b) By writing \(\sin^n x = \sin^{n-1} x \cdot \sin x\) and integrating by parts, show that \(I_n = \frac{n-1}{n} I_{n-2}\) for all \(n \ge 2\). [6]
(c) Hence prove by mathematical induction that for all \(m \in \mathbb{Z}^+\):
\[I_{2m} = \frac{(2m)!}{2^{2m}(m!)^2}\frac{\pi}{2} \qquad \text{and} \qquad I_{2m+1} = \frac{2^{2m}(m!)^2}{(2m+1)!}\] [8]
(d) Explain why \(0 < I_{2m+1} \le I_{2m} \le I_{2m-1}\) for all \(m \ge 1\), and hence show that \(\lim_{m\to\infty} \frac{I_{2m+1}}{I_{2m}} = 1\). [5]
(e) Deduce Wallis's product formula for \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and use your GDC with \(m = 5\) to approximate \(\pi\) to 3 decimal places. [5]
pool.ans: (a) I₀ = π/2, I₁ = 1, I₂ = π/4; (b) Integration by parts with u = sin^(n-1)(x), dv = sin(x)dx; (d) Squeeze theorem on 1 <= I_{2m}/I_{2m+1} <= (2m+1)/(2m)
pool.exp:

(a) \(I_0 = \int_0^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \frac{\pi}{2}\) [A1]; \(I_1 = [-\cos x]_0^{\pi/2} = 1\) [A1]; \(I_2 = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{1-\cos 2x}{2}\,dx = \frac{\pi}{4}\) [M1] [A1]
(b) Let \(u = \sin^{n-1}x \implies du = (n-1)\sin^{n-2}x\cos x\,dx\), and \(dv = \sin x\,dx \implies v = -\cos x\) [M1] [A1]
\(I_n = \left[-\sin^{n-1}x\cos x\right]_0^{\pi/2} + (n-1)\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^{n-2}x\cos^2 x\,dx = 0 + (n-1)\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^{n-2}x(1 - \sin^2 x)\,dx\) [M1] [A1]
\(I_n = (n-1)(I_{n-2} - I_n) \implies n I_n = (n-1)I_{n-2} \implies I_n = \frac{n-1}{n}I_{n-2}\) [M1] [A1] [AG]
(c) Base case \(m = 1\): \(I_2 = \frac{2!}{4(1)^2}\frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4}\) (true) [R1]. Inductive step: assume true for \(m = k\), then \(I_{2k+2} = \frac{2k+1}{2k+2}I_{2k} = \frac{(2k+2)(2k+1)}{(2k+2)^2}I_{2k} = \frac{(2k+2)!}{2^{2k+2}((k+1)!)^2}\frac{\pi}{2}\) [M1] [A1] [R1]; similarly for \(I_{2m+1}\) [M1] [A1] [A1] [A1]
(d) On \((0, \pi/2)\), \(0 < \sin x < 1 \implies \sin^{2m+1}x \le \sin^{2m}x \le \sin^{2m-1}x\) [R1] [A1]; dividing by \(I_{2m+1}\) gives \(1 \le \frac{I_{2m}}{I_{2m+1}} \le \frac{I_{2m-1}}{I_{2m+1}} = \frac{2m+1}{2m} \to 1\) by Squeeze Theorem [M1] [A1] [R1]
(e) Forming ratio \(\frac{I_{2m}}{I_{2m+1}}\) yields Wallis's product [M1] [A1] [A1]; GDC evaluation at \(m = 5\) [M1] [A1]
